content:
The Consensus API lets you search 400+ million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, over a single REST endpoint. Send a query and get back ranked papers with titles, authors, journals, publication years, citation counts, and direct links.

## Quickstart

Make your first API call in a few minutes. Every plan includes API access, and the Free plan includes 30 calls a month.

1

Sign in to Consensus

Create a free account or sign in at [consensus.app](https://consensus.app). The dashboard in the next step only opens when you’re signed in.

2

Open the API & MCP Dashboard

Go to [consensus.app/api-mcp](https://consensus.app/api-mcp/). You can also get there from your profile icon: choose **API & MCP Dashboard**.

3

Create and copy an API key

Click **Create API key**, name the key, and click **Copy API key**. The full key is shown only once, so store it somewhere safe.Already have a key? Open **Keys and clients** and click **New key**.

4

Make your first request

Save the key in an environment variable named `CONSENSUS_API_KEY`:

```
export CONSENSUS_API_KEY="paste-your-key-here"
```

Then search. `query` is the only required parameter, and the key goes in the `x-api-key` header.

You get back a JSON object with a `results` list of ranked papers. A `401` means the key is missing or wrong.

## What a response looks like

Here’s a real request and response on a paid plan, where open-access results carry full-text excerpts:

```
curl -G "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search" -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "query=what dose of creatine improves working memory"
```

```
{
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Creatine and improvement in cognitive function: Evaluation of a health claim pursuant to article 13(5) of regulation (EC) No 1924/2006",
      "authors": ["Dominique Turck", "T. Bohn", "Montaña Cámara", "…"],
      "journal_name": "EFSA Journal",
      "publisher_name": "Wiley",
      "publish_year": 2024,
      "sjr_best_quartile": 1,
      "citation_count": 5,
      "doi": "10.2903/j.efsa.2024.9100",
      "url": "https://consensus.app/papers/creatine-and-improvement-in-cognitive-function-turck-bohn/7e703e828b815257b31687a25eceac9d/",
      "takeaway": "Creatine supplementation has not been established as a cause-and-effect relationship for improving cognitive function in one or more domains.",
      "full_text_chunks": [
        "Section: Human intervention studies in healthy individuals conducted under normal conditions | Two studies had an initial loading phase of 20 g/day of creatine for 5 days, followed by 5 g/day … A significant improvement in working memory, as measured by the Backwards Digit Span test, was observed only in the study of shorter duration …",
        "Section: Weighing of the evidence | … the acute effect of creatine on working memory reported in some studies at doses of 20 g/day given for 5-7 days … was not observed at lower creatine doses, ranging from 2.2 to 14 g/day …"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Trimmed to one result with shortened excerpts. The `takeaway` gives you the paper’s conclusion; the `full_text_chunks` give you the doses and study designs behind it, each labeled with the section of the paper it came from.

## How Consensus compares

In blinded evaluations on real user queries, Consensus search returns more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See [Benchmarks](/benchmarks).

## More relevant than Google Scholar

88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers.

## Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster

More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds.

## What people build with the API

## What you can build with the Consensus API

Teams use the API to power internal research tools, field-monitoring agents, and scientific agents. Phylo calls it directly from its agents to screen about 20,000 drug targets across hundreds of diseases. Browse the use cases.

- **Internal tools:** paper search for scientific agents, field-monitoring agents, and literature tables that fill themselves.
- **Research systems:** literature review pipelines, citation-grounded writing, and recurring evidence reports.

## Full text in the API

Every search reaches inside the paper. Queries are matched against full text where available, and on paid plans each open-access result also carries the passages that answer your query, in `full_text_chunks`. To read a whole open-access paper, pass its `paper_id` to `GET /v1/papers/full_text` for its complete text as Markdown.

## Full text in the API

Excerpts and complete text: what comes back, which papers qualify, plans, and credits.

## Base URL and authentication

All requests go to:

```
https://api.consensus.app
```

Every request must include your API key in the `x-api-key` header:

```
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

See [plans and access](/api-plans-and-access) for each plan’s monthly calls, page sizes, features, and rate limits.
